problem: Long haul trucking suffers from driver shortages and safety risk; Starsky aimed to automate highway driving with remote human drivers handling the first and last miles.
business_model: Autonomous truck technology run as its own freight operation with remote driver teleoperation

founders.name: Stefan Seltz-Axmacher
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no education or employer details found in opened sources.

exit.reason: CEO said a planned $20 million Series B fell apart in November 2019 and cited timing and weak investor interest in practical safety work

competitors.name: Otto
competitors.what: Self-driving retrofit kits for long haul trucks, founded January 2016
competitors.funding_then: Reported acquisition price roughly 650 to 680 million dollars (sources differ)

competitors.name: Peloton Technology
competitors.what: Truck platooning to cut fuel use
competitors.funding_then: Reported 18 million dollars from investors including Lockheed Martin and Intel (source date not shown)

technical_complexity.rationale: Driverless highway trucking with teleoperation required safety critical software and hardware on 80,000 pound vehicles; Starsky demonstrated a driverless run in 2018 but the CEO said the technology was years from general readiness.

defensibility.rationale: Remote operation approach and safety documentation were differentiated, but the CEO said investors did not value that work.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Uber bought Otto in August 2016, signalling well funded players in the same wedge; Starsky ran out of runway when its Series B collapsed in November 2019.

market_need_then: US trucking faces driver shortages and safety costs; coverage in 2016 and 2018 showed investor appetite for self-driving trucks (Otto sale, Starsky Series A).

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised in autonomous trucking press and its shutdown post drew wide coverage, but no sourced evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Starsky raised about 21 million dollars across a 2017 seed and a 2018 Series A, then lost a planned 20 million dollar Series B in November 2019 and shut down in March 2020. The CEO blamed timing, investor fatigue with autonomy promises, and a low value placed on safety work, so the failure came from the next round not closing while the technology was still far from commercial scale.
notes: YC page lists no website; no company site fetched. The 2017 seed of 5 million rests on a Wikipedia sentence repeated by a mirror; other outlets did not name it, so treat it as less certain. Totals raised differ by source (20.25M CB Insights, 21M Robot Report, 21.7M Wikipedia and Golden). Otto source_date is the acquisition month from search results and the cited article is undated in what I saw. Name origin not found. Search summaries only; most article bodies were not opened.
